pages.text: A frog croaked in the rice field. Ribbit, ribbit! But only thick grass showed.
Dingding peered between the blades. One moved. "Something jumped there!"
Mom strode along the bank. "The frog is calling from below." "You did not even look, Mom."
She pointed down. "I know just by hearing." Off she went to the lower field.
Dingding held the bank with both hands and stepped down backward. One, two, three. "The lower patch, she said."
Below, the water was still. No grass moved. "Frog, where are you?"
Dingding looked up. Croaking came from above. Ribbit, ribbit!
Dingding climbed back up to the higher rice field and looked for the grass that had moved.
A blade moved again. Dingding crept close. A green frog sat there!
Hop! Onto Dingding's apron. Mom's voice rose from far below. "Found your frog, Dingding?"
